test_title: PYST 28: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The size of the image formed by a convex mirror _________.

options.text: is always smaller than the object
is always equal to the object
can be larger or smaller depending on object position
is always larger than the object

solution:
The correct answer is __**is always smaller than the object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex mirror**, also known as a diverging mirror, always forms a virtual, erect, and **smaller image** of the object irrespective of its position in front of the mirror.
 
• This is because convex mirrors have a **curved reflecting surface** that bulges outward, causing the reflected rays to diverge.
 
• The **image is formed behind the mirror**, and the size of the image is always reduced compared to the object's size.
 
• The nature of the image formed by a convex mirror is described using the mirror formula: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where:
 
 
• **f** = focal length (positive for convex mirrors)
 
• **v** = image distance
 
• **u** = object distance
 
 
 
• Convex mirrors are widely used as **rear-view mirrors** in vehicles because they provide a wider field of view and always produce smaller, upright images of objects, enabling drivers to see more area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Convex Mirrors:**

 
 
• Convex mirrors always produce a **virtual image** (an image that cannot be projected onto a screen).
 
• The image is always **erect (upright)** and smaller in size compared to the object.
 
• The focal length (**f**) of a convex mirror is positive because the focus lies on the same side as the reflected rays.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Convex Mirrors:**
 
 
• **Rear-view mirrors:** Used in vehicles to provide a wider field of view, helping drivers observe traffic conditions behind them.
 
• **Surveillance mirrors:** Installed in shops, warehouses, and parking lots to monitor activities in a large area.
 
• **Road safety:** Used at blind turns on roads to help drivers see oncoming traffic.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• **Concave mirrors** can produce real and inverted images or virtual and erect images depending on the object's position relative to the focal point.
 
• In contrast, convex mirrors always produce virtual, erect, and smaller images regardless of the object's position.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula and Magnification:**
 
 
• The **mirror formula** is given as: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u.
 
• The **magnification (m)** is calculated as: m = h'/h = -v/u, where:
 
 
• **h'** = height of the image
 
• **h** = height of the object
 
• **v** = image distance
 
• **u** = object distance
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Convex Mirrors in Optics:**

 
 
• Convex mirrors are part of the **spherical mirror family**, which includes concave mirrors.
 
• Their **reflective surface bulges outward**, making them ideal for producing reduced, virtual images.
 
 
 
• **Usage in Daily Life:**
 
 
• Convex mirrors are commonly seen in **public spaces** such as stores and parking lots to enhance visibility.
 
• They are crucial for **road safety** at blind spots and intersections.
